title: Reconciler Minimal Dirty Sub-tree Invalidation
problemStatement: Implement `calculateDirtySubtree(rootFiber, changedFiberId)` that traverses a tree of fiber nodes and returns a list of fiber IDs that must re-render, bailing out of branches whose props and state did not change.
interviewTrap: React's bailout mechanism skips an entire subtree only if both props AND context AND state have reference equality with workInProgress fiber counterparts.

testCases.name: Identifies changed node and non-memoized children
testCases.input: node A changes with un-memoized child B
testCases.testFn: const tree = { id: 'root', children: [{ id: 'A', children: [{ id: 'B', isMemoized: false }] }] }; return calculateDirtySubtree(tree, 'A');

testCases.name: Bails out on memoized child nodes
testCases.input: node A changes with memoized child C
testCases.testFn: const tree = { id: 'root', children: [{ id: 'A', children: [{ id: 'C', isMemoized: true }] }] }; return calculateDirtySubtree(tree, 'A');

testCases.name: Unaffected sibling branches are completely untouched
testCases.input: mutation in A does not touch branch D
testCases.testFn: const tree = { id: 'root', children: [{ id: 'A', children: [] }, { id: 'D', children: [] }] }; const dirty = calculateDirtySubtree(tree, 'A'); return dirty.includes('D');

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: The React Compiler analyzes the Control Flow Graph (CFG) at build time, identifying reactive values and automatically wrapping computations and JSX in memo caches, rendering manual useMemo and useCallback obsolete.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Fiber Invalidation Propagation & Bailout Detection.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Fiber Invalidation Propagation & Bailout Detection maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does React reconciler bailout on a clean subtree during beginWork?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: During `beginWork`, React checks two conditions: 1) `oldProps === newProps` and no state/context updates on the fiber. 2) `!includesSomeLane(wipLanes, renderLanes)`. If true, the component itself has no work. React then checks `includesSomeLane(childLanes, renderLanes)`: if false, NO descendant in the entire subtree has pending work! React calls `bailoutOnAlreadyFinishedWork()` and completely skips traversing the entire subtree in O(1) time.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The core performance bailout logic in the React reconciler engine.

realWorldUseCases.description: Skipping reconciliation on 10,000 clean fibers when an update only affects a single small component leaf.

howToExplain.opening: React achieves sub-millisecond updates in massive trees by bailing out on clean subtrees when lane priority bitmasks indicate no pending work.
keyPoints: Fiber checks if its own lanes match the current render lane.
Checks childLanes to see if any descendant needs work.
If childLanes has no matching work, skips the entire subtree in O(1).
Propagates dirty lane flags upwards during completeWork.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Lane-based dirty subtree skipping is how React renders massive applications at 60fps.
analogies: An inspection team: before entering a 50-story building, they check the sensor board in the lobby; if all green lights show on floors 10-50, they skip taking the elevator to those floors.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming React always visits every fiber node in the tree on every setState.
commonMistakes.why: React skips clean subtrees in O(1) time using childLanes bitmasks.
commonMistakes.correct: Explain that childLanes enables early bailout without tree traversal.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is bailoutOnAlreadyFinishedWork in ReactFiberBeginWork.js?
followUpDeepDive.answer: It clones the fiber's child from `current.child` to `workInProgress.child` and returns null, instructing the work loop to ascend rather than descend.
